title: IOI in the loaded gpt2 (local-full): behaviour absent, no mechanism to explain
label: null result: behaviour not present
behavior: Given 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to', the model is supposed to continue with the non-repeated name (' Mary') rather than the repeated one (' John'). Dataset task: ioi.
summary: The model loaded as gpt2 on local-full (full precision) does not do this. On 264 clean IOI prompts across two seeds its top-1 prediction was never the indirect object (accuracy 0.0); the top tokens were unrelated word pieces such as ' ali', ' Sov', ' calves'. The mean logit difference between the correct and the repeated name was 0.07 (n=64, std 1.19) and 0.12 (n=200, std 1.16), both within about 1.5 standard errors of zero and no different from the corrupted prompts (-0.15 and 0.04). The investigation was stopped after the baseline, as the protocol requires: there is no behaviour, so no circuit was searched for, no algorithm was written and no verification was attempted.

claims.text: On 64 clean IOI prompts (seed 0, local-full, full precision) top-1 accuracy is 0.0 and the mean IO-minus-S logit difference is 0.072 with std 1.19, i.e. indistinguishable from zero; the pre-registered prediction of at least 90% accuracy was refuted.

The null replicates on 200 fresh prompts (seed 1, local-full, full precision): accuracy 0.0, mean logit difference 0.123 with std 1.16 (standard error about 0.08); the pre-registered prediction that the mean lies within +/-0.3 of zero was confirmed.

Clean and corrupted prompts give the same logit difference within noise (clean 0.072 / 0.123 versus corrupt -0.151 / 0.040), so the repetition of the subject name has no measurable effect on the name preference.

limitations: Only the baseline was measured. Nothing in this report says anything about internal components.

Why the behaviour is absent was not measured. The investigation name suggests a randomly initialised null model, and the nonsense top-1 tokens are consistent with that, but no experiment here tested the weights, so this is not a finding.
A very small IO preference (below roughly 0.3 logits) cannot be excluded with 264 prompts; it would be far too weak to produce the described behaviour.
No verify_hypothesis run: there was no hypothesis about a mechanism to verify.
open_questions: Is the loaded checkpoint the trained gpt2 or a null (random-init) model? A baseline on the pretrained weights would settle whether the question applies to that model.
overall_status: unverified (no verification run) · null result: behaviour not present

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: The loaded gpt2 does the IOI behaviour: on clean prompts it prefers the non-repeated name (IO) over the repeated one (S) in the large majority of cases.

prediction.statement: The model picks IO over S on at least 90% of clean prompts.
